news.story_lead: Sabarmati-style Yamuna riverfront ‘could worsen flood risks’ in Delhi, environmentalists and others warn The letter argued that the Sabarmati model cannot be replicated along the Yamuna without accounting for the fundamental differences between the two rivers. news.full_article_text: Sabarmati-style Yamuna riverfront ‘could worsen flood risks’ in Delhi, environmentalists and others warn The letter argued that the Sabarmati model cannot be replicated along the Yamuna without accounting for the fundamental differences between the two rivers. A proposed 52-km Yamuna riverfront development project in Delhi on the lines of Ahmedabad’s Sabarmati riverfront has drawn opposition from a coalition of environmentalists, former water ministry officials, researchers and citizen groups. The 18 signatories of a letter addressed to Union jal shakti minister CR Patil, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav, Delhi lieutenant governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu and chief minister Rekha Gupta have urged the Centre and Delhi government to reconsider the plan, citing the Yamuna's different ecological and hydrological characteristics and the potential to aggravate flood risks in the capital. The objections come days after the Delhi government, on October 21, announced that it was initiating the process of signing a memorandum of understanding with the Sabarmati Riverfront Development Corporation Limited (SRFDCL) for the project. The proposed development will span 52 km in two phases – from Palla to Wazirabad in the first, and from Wazirabad to Kalindi Kunj in the second. The arguement The signatories, including former water resources secretary Shashi Shekhar, scientist Ravi Chopra and members of Yamuna Jiye Abhiyan, South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP), New Delhi Nature Society, among others, have stated that the Sabarmati is a seasonal river whose urban stretch in Ahmedabad is sustained by regulated water from the Narmada canal system and impounded by the Vasna barrage. In contrast, the Yamuna is a glacier-fed Himalayan river that carries substantial silt and experiences seasonal variations in flow. They also pointed out that most polluting drains have been diverted away from the Sabarmati riverfront stretch, an arrangement that cannot be replicated on the Yamuna, which flows through several states downstream of Delhi. The signatories warn that further construction on the Yamuna floodplain could compromise the river’s flood-carrying capacity, particularly after the floods of 2023 and 2025. The letter said that accumulated silt, encroachments, and infrastructure such as bridges, roads, and barrages had already reduced the river’s cross-sectional area, making it vulnerable to flooding at lower flows. "Notably, the floods also inundated large areas of the Delhi Development Authority’s (DDA) biodiversity parks created along the floodplain. Under such a scenario, further development in the form of a riverfront project on the floodplain without a comprehensive assessment of its cumulative impacts on the river’s flood absorption and carrying capacity has the potential to aggravate flood risks and damages in future," the communication added. The coalition also cited the National Green Tribunal’s January 2015 Mailey Se Nirmal Yamuna judgment, which rejected an earlier riverfront proposal by the Delhi Development Authority over concerns about flood-carrying capacity and floodplain protection. They have sought public disclosure of the project’s pre-feasibility report, detailed project report, cost estimates and environmental assessments. They have urged the government to prioritise restoring environmental flows, reducing pollution and completing scientific demarcation of the floodplain. "We urge the concerned Central Government Ministries and Government of Delhi to ensure that no project compromises the integrity of the Yamuna River, its floodplain and long-term flood security of the national capital. Public resources should be directed towards addressing the causes of the river’s degradation and flood risks, rather than undertaking large-scale riverfront development plans," it adds. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Paras Singh Paras Singh is a New Delhi-based journalist with Hindustan Times, where he serves as Deputy Metro Editor. He reports on urban governance, the Delhi government, the Delhi BJP, water management, the environment, communities and city life. He joined Hindustan Times in 2021 after beginning his journalism career at The Times of India in 2016, where he covered civic bodies, the water and power sectors, and urban infrastructure. Over the last decade, some of his reporting has led to significant public impact, with investigations into environmental violations, corruption and illegal industrial activity contributing to multiple judicial interventions by the National Green Tribunal and the Delhi High Court. A graduate of St. Stephen's College, University of Delhi, Paras studied journalism from the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), New Delhi. Having extensively covered the capital's evolving civic and governance landscape, his recent work increasingly explores Delhi's history, built heritage, urban evolution and the relationship between people and place, alongside continuing to report on governance and public policy. news.full_article_text: Delhi high court refuses to take suo motu cognisance of suspended ACP’s remarks on lawyers A group of lawyers urged the Delhi high court to take suo motu cognisance of the incident, saying that derogatory language was used against the legal fraternity The Delhi high court on Tuesday declined to take suo motu cognisance of the alleged misconduct and derogatory remarks made against lawyers by suspended assistant commissioner of police (ACP) Manasvi Vashishtha during a protest outside the Delhi Police Headquarters over his transfer. A bench of acting chief justice Nitin Sambre and justice Sanjay Sharma asked the lawyers to file a petition seeking action, assured them they would look into it and get the same listed. “File a formal petition; we will look into it. You file it; we will order listing. I assure you we will get listed and look into it. AAP representation dijiye, we are a court of record. What do you mean suo moto? Whatever material is there with you, let it be submitted with the registry. We assure you we will look into it," the court told the lawyers. What the lawyers asked the court Deep Dive This was after a group of lawyers urged the Delhi high court to take suo motu cognisance of the incident, saying that derogatory language was used against the legal fraternity and they were threatening to use arms such as AK-47s. “You are our chief; if you take suo motu cognisance, we will be assured,” the lawyers submitted. A protest was held outside the Delhi Police headquarters on Monday, with scores of Delhi Police officers, including the recently transferred Gandhi Nagar ACP, seeking a meeting with police commissioner Anurag Kumar over the recent face-off with Shahdara lawyers. ACP Manasvi Vashishtha was suspended following the protest. Timeline so far The controversy stems from an October 23 incident at Shahdara police station, following an alleged assault on advocate Lalit Bansal, who suffered a serious head injury. An FIR was registered on a complaint by advocate Amulya Ratan. According to the lawyers' account, several advocates visited the police station that evening to seek action against those named in the assault case. They alleged that ACP Vashishtha and the station house officer assured them that the accused, who were present at the police station, would be arrested. However, the lawyers learnt the following day that the accused had not been arrested and had reportedly been released. When the advocates returned to the police station to question the handling of the case, Vashishtha allegedly displayed his revolver and threatened and intimidated them, the bar bodies alleged. The police, however, have offered a counter-version, saying the confrontation followed a dispute between two groups over a motorcycle-related incident. A separate case was registered for alleged misbehaviour with police personnel on duty, while the allegation that the ACP pointed his service weapon at the advocates was under investigation. On Monday, the Central Delhi court bar association wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner, demanding the registration of a criminal case against Vashishtha for his alleged misconduct and derogatory remarks against lawyers during a protest outside the Delhi Police headquarters over his transfer. The bar members sought an independent and time-bound inquiry into the incident, the representation said. Meanwhile, the Rohini court bar association on Tuesday withdrew its call for an abstention from work strike, following Vashishtha’s suspension. - Lawyers Versus Police

news.headline: US Supreme Court Rejects Federal Attempt to Block 20,000 California Midterm Ballots
news.story_lead: The United States Supreme Court has dismissed an emergency injunction application by the US Department of Justice seeking to segregate 20,000 mail-in ballots in California ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The administration had claimed these ballots might belong to non-citizens, but multiple lower federal courts and state election authorities rejected the claims as inaccurate and unfeasible.
news.full_article_text:
### Overview of the Ruling
On the eve of the 2026 US midterm elections, the US Supreme Court issued a brief one-line order rejecting a request from the federal Justice Department to compel California election officials to set aside 20,000 ballots. The application, initially presented to Justice Elena Kagan and referred to the full bench, was denied, leaving earlier lower court rulings intact and concluding the administration's legal attempt to challenge these specific votes.

### Background and Federal Actions
The Department of Justice had previously dispatched formal notices to the California Secretary of State and the Los Angeles County Registrar, demanding that 20,000 registered voters be flagged over suspicions of non-citizenship. Following these communications, armed personnel from the Department of Homeland Security delivered letters directly to county electoral staff across California, threatening criminal prosecution if the identified ballots were not segregated.

### Lower Court Decisions and State Response
Prior to the Supreme Court's intervention, a federal appeals court and District Judge David Carter turned down the government's demands. In a scathing opinion, Judge Carter described the federal action as an unprecedented attempt by the executive branch to coerce state and local authorities into abandoning their constitutional electoral procedures on the eve of an election. California election officials highlighted that the dataset provided by federal authorities was riddled with inaccuracies, warning that segregating ballots during active voting was operationally unworkable and risked disenfranchising eligible voters. California remains the most populous US state, with approximately 23 million registered voters and over six million mail-in ballots already submitted prior to the ruling.

### फैसले का विवरण
2026 के अमेरिकी मध्यावधि चुनावों की पूर्व संध्या पर, अमेरिकी सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने एक पंक्ति का आदेश जारी करके न्याय विभाग के उस अनुरोध को खारिज कर दिया, जिसमें कैलिफोर्निया के चुनाव अधिकारियों को 20,000 मतपत्रों को अलग रखने का निर्देश देने की मांग की गई थी। न्यायमूर्ति एलेना कागन को प्रस्तुत और पूर्ण पीठ को संदर्भित इस याचिका को अस्वीकार कर दिया गया, जिससे निचले अदालतों के फैसले बरकरार रहे।

### संघीय कार्रवाई और पृष्ठभूमि
न्याय विभाग ने कैलिफोर्निया के सचिव और लॉस एंजिल्स काउंटी रजिस्ट्रार को पत्र भेजकर 20,000 पंजीकृत मतदाताओं को गैर-नागरिक होने के संदेह में अलग करने की मांग की थी। इसके बाद गृह सुरक्षा विभाग के अधिकारियों ने स्थानीय चुनाव कर्मचारियों को आपराधिक मुकदमों की चेतावनी देते हुए पत्र सौंपे थे।

### निचली अदालतों का रुख
सुप्रीम कोर्ट के फैसले से पहले, एक संघीय अपील अदालत और जिला न्यायाधीश डेविड कार्टर ने सरकार के अनुरोध को खारिज कर दिया था। न्यायाधीश कार्टर ने अपने फैसले में कहा कि यह चुनाव की पूर्व संध्या पर राज्यों की संवैधानिक प्रक्रियाओं में हस्तक्षेप का एक प्रयास था। कैलिफोर्निया के अधिकारियों ने बताया कि सरकार द्वारा दी गई सूची त्रुटिपूर्ण थी और मतदान के दौरान मतपत्रों को पृथक करना मतदाताओं को उनके अधिकार से वंचित कर सकता था। कैलिफोर्निया अमेरिका का सबसे अधिक आबादी वाला राज्य है, जहाँ लगभग 2.3 करोड़ पंजीकृत मतदाता हैं।

news.headline: Supreme Court Considers Plea to Relieve Judge Facing Rape Charges from Presiding Over POCSO Court
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India has agreed to examine a petition seeking the removal of an Additional District Judge facing prosecution for rape from his position as presiding officer of a POCSO court in Shamli's Kairana, Uttar Pradesh. A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notice on the survivor's plea while observing that administrative decisions regarding divesting judicial duties lie primarily with the High Court.
news.full_article_text:
### Judicial Integrity and Special Courts

The Supreme Court of India has issued notice on a petition filed by a rape survivor challenging an order of the Allahabad High Court that refused to restrain Additional District Judge (ADJ) Ashok Bhartendu from performing judicial duties as the presiding officer of a special POCSO court in Kairana, Shamli district, Uttar Pradesh.

### Bench and Court Observations

- **Bench Composition:** The matter was heard by a three-judge bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice V. Mohana.
- **Primary Mandate:** The apex court observed that deciding whether a judicial officer should be divested of judicial work falls within the administrative domain of the High Court.
- **Next Steps:** The Supreme Court indicated it could direct the Allahabad High Court to conclude its pending vigilance inquiry against the officer expeditiously. The court scheduled the next hearing for December 11, while permitting the ongoing trial proceedings to continue in accordance with law.

### Case Background and High Court Proceedings

- **High Court Decision (August 17):** A division bench of the Allahabad High Court (Justices Arindam Sinha and Satya Veer Singh) dismissed the survivor's petition for a writ of quo warranto, stating there was a presumption that the High Court administration acted appropriately and noting no allegations were raised concerning the officer's performance of judicial duties.
- **RTI Information (February 6):** An RTI reply reproduced in the High Court order revealed that on October 21, 2024, the High Court had directed the judicial officer to join the inquiry regarding an FIR registered against him.
- **Exemption:** The reply clarified that the High Court's Vigilance Bureau is exempted from the provisions of the Right to Information Act.

### Criminal Proceedings & FIR Details

- **FIR Registration:** The criminal case was lodged against the judge on December 8, 2022, at the Mayur Vihar Phase-I police station in Delhi under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), alleging rape under the pretext of a promise to marry.
- **Delhi High Court Action:** In March 2023, the Delhi High Court granted interim protection from arrest, observing prima facie that the allegations suggested a breach of promise rather than a false promise from inception. However, the High Court subsequently clarified that trial proceedings were not stayed.
- **Trial Status:** A Delhi district court took cognisance of the charges after the police filed a chargesheet in the matter.

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने उत्तर प्रदेश के शामली जिले के कैराना में पॉक्सो अदालत के पीठासीन अधिकारी के रूप में कार्यरत बलात्कार के अभियुक्त न्यायिक अधिकारी को हटाने की मांग वाली याचिका पर सुनवाई करने पर सहमति व्यक्त की है। भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्यकांत की अध्यक्षता वाली पीठ ने उत्तरजीवी की याचिका पर नोटिस जारी किया और कहा कि न्यायिक कार्यों से अलग करने का प्रशासनिक निर्णय मुख्य रूप से उच्च न्यायालय के क्षेत्राधिकार में आता है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### न्यायिक शुचिता और विशेष अदालतें

भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने बलात्कार की उत्तरजीवी द्वारा दायर एक याचिका पर नोटिस जारी किया है। इस याचिका में इलाहाबाद उच्च न्यायालय के उस आदेश को चुनौती दी गई है जिसने अतिरिक्त जिला न्यायाधीश (एडीजे) अशोक भारतेन्दु को उत्तर प्रदेश के शामली जिले के कैराना स्थित विशेष पॉक्सो अदालत के पीठासीन अधिकारी के रूप में न्यायिक कर्तव्यों का पालन करने से रोकने से इनकार कर दिया था।

### पीठ की संरचना और अदालती टिप्पणियां

- **पीठ की संरचना:** इस मामले की सुनवाई भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्यकांत, न्यायमूर्ति जॉयमाल्या बागची और न्यायमूर्ति वी. मोहना की तीन सदस्यीय पीठ ने की।
- **प्राथमिक भूमिका:** शीर्ष अदालत ने टिप्पणी की कि किसी न्यायिक अधिकारी को न्यायिक कार्य से मुक्त करने का निर्णय आदर्श रूप से उच्च न्यायालय के प्रशासनिक अधिकार क्षेत्र में आता है।
- **आगामी कदम:** सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने संकेत दिया कि वह इलाहाबाद उच्च न्यायालय को अधिकारी के खिलाफ लंबित सतर्कता जांच को शीघ्र समाप्त करने का निर्देश दे सकता है। अदालत ने अगली सुनवाई 11 दिसंबर तय की है, जबकि ट्रायल कार्यवाही को कानून के अनुसार जारी रखने की अनुमति दी है।

### मामले की पृष्ठभूमि और उच्च न्यायालय की कार्यवाही

- **उच्च न्यायालय का फैसला (17 अगस्त):** इलाहाबाद उच्च न्यायालय की खंडपीठ (न्यायमूर्ति अरिंदम सिन्हा और न्यायमूर्ति सत्य वीर सिंह) ने उत्तरजीवी की 'अधिकार-पृच्छा' (Quo Warranto) याचिका को खारिज कर दिया था। उच्च न्यायालय ने माना था कि यह माना जाएगा कि उच्च न्यायालय प्रशासन उचित कदम उठा रहा है, और याचिकाकर्ता ने जज द्वारा न्यायिक कर्तव्यों के पालन पर कोई सीधा आरोप नहीं लगाया है।
- **आरटीआई से मिली जानकारी (6 फरवरी):** उच्च न्यायालय के आदेश में उद्धृत आरटीआई उत्तर से खुलासा हुआ कि 21 अक्टूबर 2024 को उच्च न्यायालय ने न्यायिक अधिकारी को अपने खिलाफ दर्ज एफआईआर की जांच में शामिल होने का निर्देश दिया था।
- **छूट:** आरटीआई उत्तर में स्पष्ट किया गया कि उच्च न्यायालय का सतर्कता ब्यूरो सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम के दायरे से बाहर है।

### आपराधिक कार्यवाही और एफआईआर विवरण

- **एफआईआर दर्ज होना:** जज के खिलाफ आपराधिक मामला 8 दिसंबर 2022 को दिल्ली के मयूर विहार फेज-I पुलिस स्टेशन में भारतीय दंड संहिता (IPC) की धारा 376 के तहत शादी के झूठे वादे पर बलात्कार के आरोप में दर्ज किया गया था।
- **दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय की कार्रवाई:** मार्च 2023 में दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय ने गिरफ्तारी से अंतरिम राहत दी थी, यह देखते हुए कि प्रथम दृष्टया मामला शादी के वादे के उल्लंघन का प्रतीत होता है। हालांकि, बाद में उच्च न्यायालय ने स्पष्ट किया कि आपराधिक कार्यवाही पर कोई रोक नहीं है।
- **ट्रायल की स्थिति:** दिल्ली की एक जिला अदालत ने पुलिस द्वारा आरोप पत्र दाखिल करने के बाद आरोपों का संज्ञान ले लिया है।

यह याचिका इलाहाबाद उच्च न्यायालय के 17 अगस्त के उस आदेश को चुनौती देती है जिसमें अधिकार-पृच्छा याचिका खारिज कर दी गई थी।

news.headline: TRAI mandates AI-led complaint centres, 16-hour human support
news.story_lead: TRAI mandates AI-led complaint centres, 16-hour human support TRAI mandates 24/7 AI-enabled complaint centres, human support for 16 hours daily, faster appeals and penalties up to ₹ 20 lakh for mishandled cases. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has directed telecom operators and internet service providers (ISPs) to run round-the-clock complaint centres that can be handled by AI agents, while mandating human assistance for at least 16 hours a day. It has also introduced penalties of up to ₹ 20 lakh per quarter per service area for improper disposal or handling of consumer disputes, under amended telecom consumer complaint redressal rules released on Monday.
news.full_article_text: TRAI mandates AI-led complaint centres, 16-hour human support TRAI mandates 24/7 AI-enabled complaint centres, human support for 16 hours daily, faster appeals and penalties up to ₹ 20 lakh for mishandled cases. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has directed telecom operators and internet service providers (ISPs) to run round-the-clock complaint centres that can be handled by AI agents, while mandating human assistance for at least 16 hours a day. It has also introduced penalties of up to ₹ 20 lakh per quarter per service area for improper disposal or handling of consumer disputes, under amended telecom consumer complaint redressal rules released on Monday. TRAI said the rules would be published in the gazette. For the first time, the telecom regulator has included AI-based customer care services in a binding rule under the Telecom Consumer Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026. The rules, amended after more than a decade, were last revised on July 1, 2014. The amended regulation 3(3) requires AI systems to “operate with appropriate human oversight” and consumers to receive “a notification” that they are speaking to an AI agent. Under the amended rules, service providers will be charged ₹ 1,000 for every complaint and ₹ 5,000 for every appeal found to have been wrongly disposed of, with penalties capped at ₹ 20 lakh per quarter per service area. TRAI also directed operators to submit quarterly performance reports, including number of complaints and appeals received, disposed of and pending, time taken for disposal and feedback survey results, in a format specified by the regulator. Late submission of quarterly reports will attract penalties of up to ₹ 5,000 a day for 15 days and ₹ 20,000 a day thereafter, capped at ₹ 10 lakh per licensed service area. The draft regulations were released on May 7, with stakeholder comments invited until June 12 and countercomments until June 19. TRAI received 32 comments and 24 countercomments, which it uploaded to its website. An open house discussion was held on July 17. Operators opposed the 24x7 complaint-centre requirement on cost grounds. In its explanatory memorandum, TRAI said some stakeholders objected to round-the-clock operations, “citing disproportionate costs and limited benefit”. The regulator responded that the requirement “does not necessarily imply deployment of the same level of resources 24x7”. TRAI received 73,081 complaints in 2025-26, up from 44,733 in 2023-24, pointing to dissatisfaction with operators’ grievance redressal systems. Some stakeholders have also questioned whether TRAI can impose penalties through regulations. The penalties under the current rule are new, however the regulator has been imposing financial disincentives under the Standards of Quality of Service of Access (Wireline and Wireless) and Broadband (Wireline and Wireless) Service Regulations, 2024. This was also a concern for some stakeholders who said this may result in double penalties on telecom service providers. But TRAI said the two serve “distinct regulatory objectives”. The telecom regulator has also scrapped the advisory committees and replaced them with oversight committees in every service provider to oversee and periodically review the functioning of its grievance redressal mechanism. Consumer groups, who sent 22 of the 32 comments on the draft, opposed the move, with one saying it makes the system “operator reviewing operator”. TRAI said the committees caused delays, making the appellate process inadequate. Appeal timelines have also been halved, with consumers getting 15 days instead of 30 to appeal and the appellate authority is required to decide within 15 days. Helplines must use a standard IVRS menu with separate options for complaints, appeals and queries, along with a human option and a call-back facility. Complaints can be registered through apps and websites, with status updates by SMS and email, and service must be offered in a state official language besides Hindi and English. After every closed complaint, consumers will be asked to rate the resolution from 1 to 5, and the results will be published quarterly. Disputes must be resolved through a non-chargeable numbers instead of a dedicated toll-free system, providers must set up dedicated desks and accessible apps for persons with disabilities, and records must be kept for six months, up from three. ISPs with 10,000 or fewer subscribers are exempt from the rules, which consumer groups said leaves small-town and rural users without a remedy. Satellite service providers are also covered under the rules, while OTT services are outside TRAI’s jurisdiction. The rules take effect 30 days after Gazette publication. news.full_article_text: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh, triggers heavy rain; thousands evacuated, coastal areas on alert Andhra Pradesh had stepped up evacuation and disaster management measures ahead of the cyclone's arrival. Severe cyclonic storm Murasu made landfall along the south Andhra Pradesh coast early Tuesday, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds to the region. The storm crossed the coastline near Ongole in Prakasam district at around 1am, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). Track live updates The cyclone made landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, after moving across the west-central Bay of Bengal. It brought sustained wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph, according to the IMD's forecast before landfall. The storm comes less than a week after Cyclone Arnab affected parts of India's eastern coast. Lakhs evacuated across Andhra and Odisha Deep Dive Andhra Pradesh had stepped up evacuation and disaster management measures ahead of the cyclone's arrival. Around 2,000 people had been evacuated from vulnerable coastal areas, with the administration planning to move approximately 30,000 people to safer locations, as per PTI. Earlier, over 1.6 lakh people were evacuated from five vulnerable districts of Odisha by 6 pm on Monday ahead of cyclone Murasu's landfall, with Ganjam accounting for around 1.5 lakh of those evacuated. At least 1.4 lakh more people are expected to be moved to safer locations as the state steps up its preparations to deal with the cyclone, HT has learnt. Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu had directed officials to remain on high alert and ensure that rescue, relief and restoration arrangements were in place. The state government had also taken precautionary measures to protect irrigation infrastructure, reservoirs and agricultural land. Around 31,000 electricity poles had been dispatched to facilitate restoration work in case the storm damaged power infrastructure. The administration is now assessing the extent of damage to electricity networks, roads, houses and crops. Heavy rain forecast across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana The IMD had forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places across coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema, with extremely heavy rainfall possible at isolated locations. Telangana was also expected to receive heavy rainfall as the weather system moves inland after crossing the coast. Parts of Tamil Nadu, south Odisha and Chhattisgarh were also under a weather alert. The weather department has warned that rainfall activity could continue even after landfall, as the cyclone weakens and moves inland. Flights, trains disrupted due to cyclone Cyclone Murasu disrupted air and rail services ahead of its landfall. At least 30 domestic flights were cancelled on Monday across Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Tirupati and Chennai airports because of adverse weather conditions. Railway authorities also cancelled nine trains as a precautionary measure ahead of the cyclone's arrival. Passengers have been advised to check with airlines and railway authorities for updated schedules and service information. Odisha, Tamil Nadu step up relief measures Odisha had moved more than 1.6 lakh people to safer locations as a precaution, with several southern districts placed on alert. Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri were among the districts expected to receive heavy rainfall. Rescue teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) and fire services were kept ready for emergency operations. Tamil Nadu had also extended assistance to Andhra Pradesh by sending three NDRF teams comprising 90 personnel and electricity department teams with 500 personnel to support rescue and power restoration work. The back-to-back cyclones have raised concerns over further damage to agriculture and infrastructure, particularly in areas still recovering from Cyclone Arnab. Storm surge, fishermen warned against venturing into sea Before landfall, the IMD had warned of a storm surge of around 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide in low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh. The warning covered vulnerable stretches of the coast, including parts of Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts. Fishermen had been advised not to venture into the sea, with rough conditions expected over the west-central Bay of Bengal and along the Andhra Pradesh coast. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement that an annual review had found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme's eligibility requirements.
news.full_article_text: Last year, Trump accused South Africa of white genocide in a meeting with President Cyril Ramaphosa at the White House - Published 2 hours ago US President Donald Trump has notified Congress of his intention to remove South Africa and Rwanda from a preferential trade programme, from 1 January 2027. The African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) allows eligible African countries to export thousands of products to the US duty-free. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement that an annual review had found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme's eligibility requirements. He added that the Trump administration had additionally notified the two countries of the decision. The Trump administration cited barriers to US trade and investment, as well as concerns over national security and foreign policy interests in the region. In Rwanda's case, Washington also raised concerns about human rights, political pluralism, the rule of law and workers' rights. The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by US Treasury for its alleged role in the armed rebellion in eastern DR Congo. The US Treasury said Rwanda's defence ministry directed thousands of troops to fight alongside M23 rebels in eastern DR Congo, providing weapons, equipment, logistics and training. For South Africa, the US additionally pointed to corruption. "The Trump administration is working to ensure our African partners take the necessary steps to meet the eligibility criteria," Greer said. The announcement comes amid strained relations between Washington and both countries, with the proposed termination threatening their access to preferential trade arrangements with the US. Last year, Trump accused South Africa of white genocide in a meeting with President Cyril Ramaphosa at the White House and launched a US refugee pathway for Afrikaners. US Ambassador to South Africa Leo Brent Bozell III said it was regrettable that South African policies led to its termination from Agoa. "This was a predictable and preventable outcome resulting from the rejection by South Africa's government of real concerns raised by the US," he wrote on X. Related topics

news.story_lead: Meghalaya: Paul Lyngdoh returns as minister; Metbah quits cabinet after UDP collapse The development marks a major reversal for the UDP, which won 12 seats in the 2023 assembly elections and emerged as a significant regional force Meghalaya’s United Democratic Party (UDP) president Metbah Lyngdoh lost his cabinet berth following the political upheaval that reduced his party to a one-man outfit. Meanwhile, former party colleague Paul Lyngdoh returned to the Conrad K Sangma government as a minister, this time representing the National People’s Party (NPP). news.full_article_text: Meghalaya: Paul Lyngdoh returns as minister; Metbah quits cabinet after UDP collapse The development marks a major reversal for the UDP, which won 12 seats in the 2023 assembly elections and emerged as a significant regional force Meghalaya’s United Democratic Party (UDP) president Metbah Lyngdoh lost his cabinet berth following the political upheaval that reduced his party to a one-man outfit. Meanwhile, former party colleague Paul Lyngdoh returned to the Conrad K Sangma government as a minister, this time representing the National People’s Party (NPP). Paul, the West Shillong legislator who left the UDP for the NPP along with two other party colleagues, was sworn in as a cabinet minister by governor CH Vijayashankar at Lok Bhavan on Monday evening. He was allocated the tourism portfolio, which he previously held before being dropped in the September 2025 cabinet reshuffle. His induction follows Metbah’s resignation from the cabinet on October 31, after 11 of the UDP’s 12 legislators left the party, with eight joining the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and three moving to the NPP. Metbah, who held the power, water resources, taxation and textiles portfolios, submitted his resignation to chief minister Conrad K Sangma with immediate effect, saying he could no longer continue as a minister after being left as the party’s sole legislator. “After very thorough and careful consideration, I have taken the decision that I will not be able to continue as Cabinet minister in the MDA government,” he said, adding that his resignation was the first decision taken by the party and that further decisions would follow. The development marks a major reversal for the UDP, which won 12 seats in the 2023 assembly elections and emerged as a significant regional force. The speaker formally recognised the merger of eight legislators with the BJP on October 16, followed by the recognition of the merger of three others with the NPP on October 23. The BJP’s strength consequently rose from two to 10, while the NPP increased its tally from 33 to 36. The UDP was left with Metbah as its sole MLA. The political crisis was building since September, when eight legislators — Lahkmen Rymbui, Pius Marwein, Kyrmen Shylla, Mayralborn Syiem, Matthew Beyondstar Kurbah, Ollan Singh Suin, Balajied Kupar Synrem and Synshar Kupar Roy Lyngdoh Thabah — joined the BJP. They cited assurances on long-pending regional issues, including the inclusion of Khasi and Garo languages in the Constitution’s Eighth Schedule, implementation of the Meghalaya Residents Safety and Security Act, coal mining and the relocation of the Harijan Colony from Them Iew Mawlong. The subsequent departure of Paul, Renikton Lyngdoh Tongkhar and Nujorki Sungoh to the NPP virtually wiped out the UDP’s legislative presence. Metbah had earlier expressed surprise at the mass exodus, questioning why legislators elected on UDP tickets had abandoned the party. He maintained that the organisation continued to exist despite the defections and said it would prepare for the 2028 Assembly elections. Metbah insisted that his resignation was not taken under pressure. “I will never take any decision under pressure because under pressure you will make lots of mistakes,” he said, adding that the party’s Central Executive Committee will decide whether the UDP would continue supporting the MDA government. The issue is expected to be discussed at the party’s November 3 meeting. Paul, meanwhile, said he had neither demanded nor suggested any particular portfolio. He said the chief minister wanted continuity in the Tourism Department and asked him to take charge. “I gladly accepted, considering the challenges that have emerged over the past few days,” he said. He said his immediate priority would be to put the department back on track, consult stakeholders and review tourism projects, while strengthening safety arrangements for visitors and residents. As the UDP struggles to chart a future with its president as its only legislator, one of its former senior leaders returned to the cabinet under the banner of the party that absorbed him. For Metbah, the November 3 meeting could prove crucial in determining the UDP’s next political course, including its position within the ruling MDA coalition. For Paul, the return to office marks a fresh chapter in a political realignment that has fundamentally altered Meghalaya’s regional party landscape.

Taking a swipe at the INDIA bloc's 'Vote Bachao' rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, Shah dubbed it a 'Ghuspetiya Bachao' rally (save infiltrators). "Now comes what causes stomach ache for Rahul Gandhi. Three crore votes are those that do not exist. They are Bangladeshi infiltrators. Three crore people are those who do not exist. They are not present. These three crore are infiltrators. Tell me, who are these three crore people? Should they be removed or not? Rahul ji says don't remove," Shah said, adding, "we will remove each and every infiltrator from the electoral rolls." Referring to Congress's allegation that BJP won because of SIR, he asked whether BJP's win in the 2014 and 2019 polls was because of SIR when the exercise was not conducted. On the mock parliament held in Delhi, he said Rahul Gandhi should have taken the role of Prime Minister in the mock parliament. "Shall I say why? Because in real Parliament, he (Rahul Gandhi) will never be able to become PM...so, it will bring peace to Sonia Gandhi's heart," Shah said, adding Congress was no match for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's popularity. Taking potshots at Rahul Gandhi's foreign trips "every three-four months", Shah said one needs to work hard and resolve people's problems. Congress claims credit when it wins elections, but blames EVMs when it loses, he said and recalled a Hindi idiom about a worker blaming his tools to hide his inability to deliver results. Congress party resorted to " ₹ 12 lakh crore corruption in 10 years of its tenure," while there are no allegations of graft during the twelve-year tenure of PM Modi. Citing Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Gujarat, Tripura and Odisha, he said Congress has not been in power in these states for decades; Shah asked Rahul Gandhi if this was because of the SIR. The Union Home Minister further attacked Congress, saying Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy has made the state an "ATM for Congress leaders of Delhi Durbar". While Congress failed to implement its poll 'guarantees' in Telangana, PM Modi fulfilled promises of abrogation of Article 370, construction of Ram temple at Ayodhya, ending triple talaq and finishing terrorism and naxalism, and the Centre is now promising to make the country 'drug-free.' Only the BJP can stop the corruption and the "conspiracy to sell Telangana," and not the BRS or the AIMIM. Shah carried the national flag during the foot march and was accompanied by Union Coal Minister Kishan Reddy, Union MoS (Home) Bandi Sanjay Kumar, and other Telangana BJP leaders. The foot march began at the Babu Jagjivan Ram statue, and it will conclude at Mozamjahi Market. Shah arrived at Begumpet Airport here on Monday afternoon to participate in the padayatra. On November 1, it had spent most of that time over Punjab and Haryana, passing over dozens of fires that the satellites had spotted in the day before. On October 28, it came in from the east, away from the fire belt, and passed few fires. On October 18, it crossed Punjab, but before the evening burning had begun, and the city stayed comparatively clean. Humidity was above 90% on the nights of October 31 and November 1, against 76% on October 28. But it was just as humid on October 31 as on November 1, and the afternoon air on November 1 was far dirtier.
